bank_kyc.q: To open a bank account, what does KYC need?
bank_kyc.b: Proof of identity, proof of address and a photo
bank_kyc.c: Updating details through a link the bank sends by SMS
bank_kyc.why: KYC checks who you are with ID, address proof and a photo, at the branch or in the bank's official app. Banks never ask you to update KYC through an SMS link.

bank_type.q: You want to keep your allowance safe and earn a little interest. Which account?
bank_type.c: No account: cash at home is safer
bank_type.why: A savings account is for keeping money and earns interest. Current accounts are for businesses and usually pay none.

bank_pin.q: Who is allowed to know your UPI PIN?
bank_pin.a: A bank officer who calls about fraud
bank_pin.why: Nobody else ever needs your PIN or OTP. A caller asking for it is a scammer, however official they sound.

bank_receive.q: A buyer sends you a QR code to "receive" ₹1,500 for your old cycle. What do you do?
bank_receive.a: Scan it and enter your PIN to receive the money
bank_receive.b: Refuse: you never need your PIN to receive money
bank_receive.c: Scan it but enter a wrong PIN to be safe
bank_receive.why: A PIN is only ever needed to send money. Scanning a code and entering your PIN would pay them.

budget_needs.q: Which of these is a need?
budget_needs.a: A monthly bus pass to get to school
budget_needs.why: Needs are what you must have to live, study and work. Transport to school is a need; the others are wants.

budget_rule.q: In the 50/30/20 rule, what is the 20% for?
budget_rule.why: About 50% for needs, 30% for wants and 20% for saving, with saving planned first.

budget_sale.q: Sneakers are "₹3,600, now ₹1,800!" You weren't planning to buy shoes. If you buy them, you have...
budget_sale.why: A sale only saves money on something you were going to buy anyway. Otherwise it's just spending.

budget_first.q: What's the most reliable way to save every month?
budget_first.a: Move savings out as soon as money arrives, automatically if possible
budget_first.b: Save whatever is left at the end of the month
budget_first.c: Save only in months when you feel rich
budget_first.why: Pay yourself first. At the end of the month there's usually nothing left.

save_emergency.q: Your needs cost ₹800 a month. A good starting emergency fund is about...
save_emergency.why: Aim for 3–6 months of needs, kept somewhere you can reach quickly, like a savings account.

save_compound.q: Why does starting to save early matter so much?
save_compound.a: Banks pay young people a special rate
save_compound.b: It doesn't, only the amount matters
save_compound.c: Compound interest earns interest on interest, so time multiplies growth
save_compound.why: With compounding, the longer money grows, the faster it grows. Time is the secret ingredient.

save_72.q: Using the rule of 72, about how long does money take to double at 8% a year?
save_72.why: 72 ÷ 8 = 9. The same rule shows how fast a debt doubles at high interest.

save_inflation.q: Your savings earn 3.5% a year while prices rise 6% a year. What's happening to your money?
save_inflation.a: It's growing, so all is fine
save_inflation.b: It buys a little less each year
save_inflation.why: If interest is lower than inflation, your real return is negative: the same money buys less.

debt_total.q: Two loans for ₹30,000: 12 months at ₹2,665 EMI, or 24 months at ₹1,412 EMI. Which costs less in total?
debt_total.a: 24 months, because the EMI is smaller
debt_total.why: A longer tenure lowers the EMI but adds interest. Always compare the total you'll pay.

debt_minimum.q: You owe ₹10,000 on a credit card and pay only the minimum each month. What happens?
debt_minimum.a: Nothing bad: the minimum is enough
debt_minimum.c: Interest of over 40% a year keeps the debt alive for years
debt_minimum.why: Card interest is around 3–4% a month on what you don't pay. Pay the full bill whenever you can.

debt_score.a: Paying every EMI and card bill on time
debt_score.c: Missing a payment and paying double next month
debt_score.why: On-time repayment builds your score. A good score means cheaper loans later.

debt_app.q: An app offers ₹5,000 instantly with no checks if you allow access to your contacts. This is...
debt_app.b: A likely predatory loan app: huge fees, high interest and harassment
debt_app.c: The same as a bank loan
debt_app.why: Only borrow from regulated lenders, and never give an app your contacts or photos.

inv_bond.q: When you buy a town bond, you are...
inv_bond.a: Lending the town money for a fixed time at a fixed interest rate
inv_bond.b: Buying a piece of the town
inv_bond.why: A bond is a loan from you to a government or company. Owning a piece of a company is a stock.

inv_diversify.q: What's the safest way to invest ₹5,000 in the stock market?
inv_diversify.a: All in the one company everyone is talking about
inv_diversify.c: Spread across many companies, for example an index fund
inv_diversify.why: Diversification means one company's crash can't sink you.

inv_horizon.q: You need money for exam fees in 3 months. Where should it be?
inv_horizon.b: In a savings account or short FD
inv_horizon.why: Money needed soon belongs somewhere safe. Stocks can be down exactly when you need them.

inv_crash.q: Your index fund falls 15% in a month. You don't need the money for years. A sensible move?
inv_crash.a: Stay invested and keep your monthly SIP going
inv_crash.b: Sell everything before it falls more
inv_crash.c: Borrow money to buy a single hot stock
inv_crash.why: Selling in a panic locks in the loss. Long-term investors ride out falls.

inv_etf.q: What's the main advantage of an index fund or ETF?
inv_etf.c: It's diversified and has low fees
inv_etf.why: Index funds hold the whole market cheaply. Nothing in the market is guaranteed.

inv_risk.q: An investment promises much higher returns than an FD. That usually means...
inv_risk.c: It has no risk at all
inv_risk.why: Higher possible returns come with higher risk. "High return, no risk" is a red flag.

safe_ponzi.q: "Double Dhamaka" pays its first members exactly on time. Where does that money come from?
safe_ponzi.b: Money paid in by newer members
safe_ponzi.why: A Ponzi scheme pays old members with new members' money until it collapses.

safe_insurance.q: Why pay a small insurance premium every month?
safe_insurance.a: To avoid a huge loss if disaster strikes
safe_insurance.c: It's a waste unless something happens
safe_insurance.why: Insurance trades a small certain cost for protection from a big uncertain loss.

safe_report.q: You've just been scammed through UPI. First thing to do?
safe_report.a: Wait a few days and hope it comes back
safe_report.b: Pay the scammer more to "unlock" a refund
safe_report.c: Call your bank and the cybercrime helpline 1930 right away
safe_report.why: Report fast to your bank and to 1930 / cybercrime.gov.in. Speed gives the best chance of recovery.

safe_job.q: "Earn ₹5,000 a day! Pay ₹500 to register." What's the tell?
safe_job.a: A real job never asks you to pay to join
safe_job.b: ₹500 is a small fee for a big salary
safe_job.c: It's fine if they paid a friend first
safe_job.why: Real jobs pay you. Task scams pay small amounts first to win trust, then ask for more.

safe_real.q: An FD pays 7% a year and inflation is 6%. Your real return is about...
